subject: Data handling: model training & deletion windows
messages:
From: David Lee <david.lee@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: security@greenlinehealth.com, procurement@greenlinehealth.com
Date: Sun, 21 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data handling: model training & deletion windows

Mina —

Thanks for the quick intro at yesterday's workshop. Before we proceed with the pilot, our legal and security teams need explicit, operational answers on two things:

1) Training usage: We need a clear statement of whether Greenline Health customer payloads (API calls, attachments, prompts) are ever used to train or fine-tune Redwood models, including any aggregated or derivative learning pipelines. Please include any conditional cases (e.g., opt-ins, research programs, anonymized telemetry).

2) Deletion/retention lifecycle: Describe the end-to-end deletion flow, including how long copies (logs, backups, debug snapshots, cached KV states) are retained, tombstone handling, and how long it might take for data to be fully purged from backups and third-party snapshots. We also need to understand where copies might live (cloud provider backups, internal debug buckets) and whether those are covered by the same deletion guarantees.

Can you provide an operational-level reply (not just marketing language) and an attestation we can sign-off against? Procurement would like to include that language in our SOW.

Thanks,
David
Lead, Security Operations
Greenline Health
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: David Lee <david.lee@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@greenlinehealth.com, marcussales@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data handling: model training & deletion windows

David — thanks for the clear asks. Below is an operational summary; I attached an attestation PDF and a short diagram of our erase pipeline for reference. If you want a fully executed certificate, Marcus (copied on thread) will coordinate Legal.

Operational guarantees (short version):

- Model training: Redwood does NOT use customer-provided content to train or fine-tune our public/hosted models unless a customer explicitly opts in via a written commercial agreement or feature flag. For Dedicated and Private deployments (reserved capacity or VPC/on-prem), the default is that data never leaves the customer's designated environment and is not used for model training.

- Telemetry & aggregated metrics: We collect minimal telemetry (errors, latency histograms) for service health. Aggregated system metrics are anonymized and cannot be reverse-engineered to recreate customer prompts. Customer-identifying telemetry is retained for troubleshooting only and is purged per the retention windows below unless specifically preserved under a legal hold.

- Retention & delete flow (typical hosted configuration):
  • Primary request logs: retained 30 days by default; configurable in enterprise plans.
  • Debug snapshots & ephemeral traces: retained up to 7 days; these are time-limited and explicitly excluded from training pipelines.
  • KV/cache state: in-memory caches are evicted at session end; any persisted cache is treated as customer data and follows the same delete lifecycle.
  • Backups & snapshots: our managed provider backups are kept for disaster recovery for up to 90 days. We maintain a tombstone index to mark deleted objects; tombstoned data is removed from live indices within 48 hours, but physical deletion from backups may take the full backup retention window (up to 90 days).
  • Archive/long-term retention: only occurs when contracted (e.g., for compliance) and is explicitly listed in your SOW.

- Erase pipeline: delete request -> tombstone -> index purge -> metadata purge -> backup expiration. We include verification checks and provide a deletion confirmation token. See attached erase_pipeline_diagram.png.

- Exceptions & third parties: Copies that we store with third-party providers (cloud storage snapshots, vendor analytics) are covered by our contractual controls; we convey deletion instructions and enforce retention via lifecycle rules. However, physical deletion timing can depend on provider snapshot schedules — we commit to ensuring no model training or derivative use of customer content during those windows.

What I can attach today: a non-training attestation PDF (signed by Redwood Security), an erase pipeline diagram, and a short table of configurable retention parameters for enterprise customers. If Greenline needs a custom deletion SLA (e.g., reduce backup retention to 30 days), we can include that in the SOW and coordinate the deployment plan.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus will loop in Legal to provide a signed attestation template you can include in the SOW.
2) If you need an amended retention window for backups, let us know target numbers and we will scope impact on DR.

Happy to jump on a quick call with your security team if that helps.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: David Lee <david.lee@greenlinehealth.com>

Mina — appreciate the detailed operational summary. A couple follow-ups:

- Will the attestation explicitly state 'Customer data will not be used for model training or evaluation' in plain language? Our auditors prefer concrete phrasing rather than caveats.

- For backups: does Redwood have the ability to shorten the backup retention window for a named customer in the hosted configuration? If not, what controls can we add (e.g., encrypted object lifecycle managed by customer keys) to ensure our data is unrecoverable after deletion?

- Regarding telemetry: can you confirm whether request/response pairs may ever be stored beyond debug windows for support tickets? If so, how are they isolated and redacted?

Procurement prefers a signed letter rather than a self-service PDF. If Legal at Redwood can draft an attestation with the wording above and a proposed deletion SLA (timeline for final purge from backups), that should be sufficient to proceed.

Thanks — can Marcus or someone on your side own the attestation draft?

David
